# Copilot Instructions

## Project scope and sources of truth

- This repository builds a Home Assistant Lovelace **custom frontend card** `custom:ha-dum-dashboard`, distributed through HACS: the control centre of the house (what needs the user, what runs now, the controls by group).
- `CURRENT_SPEC.md` and `DESIGN_HISTORY.md` of this card are in the private repository `ha-config` (`dum/`), next to this repository; references "CURRENT_SPEC.md, section" in code and tests point there. `ENTITY_MAP.md` (`ha-config/dum/`) lists the confirmed entities.
- `CURRENT_SPEC.md` defines intended behavior and contains only decisions the user made. `DESIGN_HISTORY.md` is history only and never binding. There is no `TODO.md`, `AUDIT.md` or `IDEAS.md`: anything the user has not decided is a question for the user in the chat.
- Do not invent entity IDs, attributes, units, values of states or Home Assistant behavior. Anything not confirmed by the snapshot `ha-config/ha/entities.json` or by the user stays optional or becomes a question.
- The spec includes features that are not implemented yet. Implement only the requested scope; do not claim a specified feature exists just because it is documented.

## Product behavior to preserve

- Mobile first: iPhone 14 Pro at 393 × 852, no horizontal scrolling from 320 px, every interactive element at least 44 × 44 px, dark and light mode, no axe violations.
- Everything on the first screen that switches something is protected: it acts on a hold or a double tap, one tap only shows the hint. Nothing moves or changes its size because of a hint. A tile with a chevron only opens a detail and acts on one tap.
- Missing, `unknown` and `unavailable` values are not alarms and are never counted as a state (a blind without data is in no preset).
- The washing machine, the dryer and the cooker hood can never be switched off from this card.
- The card speaks Czech, English and Swedish (`src/translations/cs.ts` is the source and its type is the contract); a change of a text updates all three in the same commit.

## Shared kit

- Everything shared with the other cards lives in `michal-madle/ha-dashboard-kit`, pinned to a commit in `package.json`: tiles and the other controls, the protected gesture, languages and formats, the rules of the configuration, the test tooling.
- Code or a rule that more cards need is created in the kit, never copied here. Never edit the kit inside `node_modules`.

## Implementation conventions

- Strict TypeScript with Lit 3: `src/index.ts` registers the element; `src/ha-dum-dashboard.ts` is the card; `src/config.ts` validates the YAML into `Settings`; `src/styles.ts` holds the look; `src/translations/` the texts.
- Home Assistant is called only through `call()` of the card, so a failed call shows in the card.
- `examples/dum.yaml` contains every key with its default; the tests load it as the configuration of every scenario.
- `ha-dum-dashboard.js` in the root is generated by `npm run build` and committed for HACS; never edit it by hand.

## Tests

- `npm test` builds the card and runs Playwright on `tests/harness.html` with the scenarios of `tests/scenarios.js` (a fake `hass`). Every behavior of the spec that is implemented has a test; nothing is reported as passed that did not run.
